areas.name: Connect and Ingest Data into Data 360
Model and Prepare Data in Data 360
Build Analytics Assets in Tableau Next

papers.name: foundation
papers.title: Foundation: orientation across Tableau Next, Semantics and Data 360
papers.audience: Someone new to the stack, or an account-side reader who needs to talk about it credibly. Vocabulary, what each feature is, and which tool is the right one to reach for.

papers.name: practitioner
papers.title: Practitioner: delivering the core pipeline
papers.audience: Someone building on the platform. How the pieces connect, what each stage produces for the next, and the constraints that change a design.

papers.name: advanced
papers.title: Advanced: the person the team escalates to
papers.audience: Edge behaviour, exact limits, interactions between features, and the facts stated only in passing inside a procedure step or a Note.

papers.name: core-pipeline
papers.title: Core pipeline only: can you run a delivery
papers.audience: Tier-1 areas only - get data in, model it, add semantics, build assets, deliver them. Mixed level. Nothing peripheral.

papers.name: role-admin
papers.title: Salesforce admin: setting up and running Tableau Next
papers.audience: Enablement, permission sets and licences, feature setup, governance and auditing.

papers.name: role-data-engineer
papers.title: Data engineer: from source system to semantic model
papers.audience: Ingestion, data lake and model objects, transforms, and the semantic layer beneath the analytics.

papers.name: role-analyst
papers.title: Analyst and author: building and sharing the analytics
papers.audience: Semantic models as consumed, visualizations, dashboards, metrics, and getting them to users.

papers.name: role-architect
papers.title: Architect: shape, limits and lifecycle
papers.audience: How the platform constrains a design, how work moves between orgs, and what the licence and limit picture looks like.

papers.name: buried-facts
papers.title: Buried facts: what the documentation only says in passing
papers.audience: Every item here rests on a fact stated inside a procedure step, a table or a Note callout rather than in a feature overview. A hard paper, and the one that separates people who have really used the product.
